channel.title: daryo
channel.description: Regional headlines in English, updated four times a day.

item.title: Almaty City Hall Denies Reduction in Bus Service Amid Passenger Complaints
item.description: Almaty's city hall stated that the number of buses on routes has not decreased, despite passenger complaints about longer waiting times. The administration attributes delays to traffic congestion and a significant percentage of passengers not paying fares, which distorts route load data.

item.title: Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan Agree to Increase Flights Between Countries
item.description: Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan have agreed to increase the number of authorized flights between their major cities. Agreements reached in Tashkent will raise weekly frequencies on the Almaty-Tashkent and Astana-Tashkent routes to 60 flights each. Other routes will see frequencies increase from 14 to 20 flights per week.

item.title: Majority of Kazakhstanis Earn Less Than 200,000 Tenge Monthly, Data Shows
item.description: A significant portion of Kazakhstan's population, 61%, earns a monthly salary of 187,000 tenge, falling short of 200,000 tenge. Despite the national average monthly wage exceeding 486,000 tenge in the second half of the year, economists note employers are hesitant to raise wages, citing a readily available workforce at current rates. Regional disparities exist, with East Kazakhstan and Atyrau regions reporting higher average salaries.

item.title: Turkey's Ruling Party: Russia Does Not Meet Requirements for Observer Status in Turkic States Organization
item.description: Turkey's ruling Justice and Development Party (AK Parti) believes Russia does not meet the criteria for observer status in the Organization of Turkic States (OTS). According to party official Kürşad Zorlu, the OTS charter requires a Turkic or related language to be a state or official language across the entire territory of an applicant country. Russia's potential application is being considered under an "OTS+" cooperation format.

item.title: Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan Agree to Increase Flights Between Countries
item.description: Aviation authorities from Kazakhstan and Uzbekistan have agreed to increase flight frequencies between Almaty-Tashkent and Astana-Tashkent routes to 60 flights per week for each route. The agreement was reached in Tashkent during a conference on civil aviation cooperation within the C5+1 framework. This aims to enhance connectivity and cooperation between the two Central Asian nations.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's construction firms to require charter capital up to 100 million soms
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Construction announced that building companies will be required to have charter capital of up to 100 million soms. These funds will serve as a financial guarantee for homebuyers, especially in cases of developer bankruptcy or misconduct. Minister Nurdane Oruntaev stated this capital will remain with the firm until construction completion.

item.title: Tashkent City Hall seeks McKinsey & Company to improve urban management system
item.description: Tashkent City Hall plans to engage the international consulting firm McKinsey & Company to enhance its urban management system. Discussions were held with a delegation led by Bob Sternfels, global managing partner, focusing on the 'Tashkent 2030' development program and strategic initiatives. The collaboration will also cover training city service personnel.

item.title: Kazakhstan Ministry Denies Rumors of Tax on Bank Deposit Interest
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of National Economy has clarified that there are no plans to introduce a tax on interest earned from individual bank deposits. The ministry stated that current tax code provisions exempt such income from personal income tax.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Introduces New Regulations for Private Aircraft and Helicopters
item.description: Kyrgyzstan has updated its aviation rules for private aircraft and helicopters engaged in international flights outside commercial air transport. The new regulations aim to align national standards with international safety requirements, including enhanced pilot training and aircraft maintenance.

item.title: Kazakhstan Activist Reports Abuse of Pension Seizure by Bailiffs
item.description: An activist in Kazakhstan's Abai Region has appealed to President Tokayev regarding alleged abuse by private bailiffs who reportedly withheld an elderly woman's entire pension for six years. The activist claims the funds have been returned after public outcry, and legal action is pending.

item.title: Kyrgyz journalist summoned for questioning by police
item.description: Kyrgyz journalist Ernis Kiyaz reported on Facebook that he was invited for a conversation by a police officer. Kiyaz initially refused to come to the station but agreed to a meeting at a neutral location. He has recently been producing podcasts on various topics, including politics, and has interviewed several political figures.

item.title: Uzbekistan introduces fines for illegal interference in construction permits
item.description: Individuals illegally interfering with the permit process for urban development activities in Uzbekistan may face fines of up to 132 million UZS. First-time offenders could receive a fine or up to 15 days of detention. Repeat offenses carry heavier penalties, including imprisonment for up to two years.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan's Construction Ministry urges buyers to check new buildings via QR code
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Construction is encouraging apartment buyers to verify the legality of new buildings using QR codes found on property passports. The QR codes link to the ministry's website, providing details on land documents, project expertise, and permits. This initiative aims to simplify information access for citizens.

item.title: Uzbekistan Introduces New Rules for Compensation for Disaster Victims
item.description: Uzbekistan has established a new procedure for assessing and compensating damages to life, health, and property resulting from technogenic emergencies. New compensation funds will be created at local government levels, funded by local budgets and other non-prohibited sources. The Ministry of Emergency Situations is tasked with developing rules for compensating legal entities.

item.title: Kazakhstan Considers Decriminalizing Economic Offenses for Businesses
item.description: Kazakhstan's President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev proposed decriminalizing economic offenses, aiming to distinguish between honest mistakes and intentional violations. An economist suggests unclear legal norms lead to differing interpretations, causing businesses to face criminal prosecution. Clearer rules and a unified approach are needed to ensure entrepreneurs are held accountable only for proven violations.

item.title: Qashqadaryo Recalculates 2.3 Billion Soums in Heating Fees for Unserved Periods
item.description: In Qashqadaryo, Uzbekistan, approximately 2.3 billion soums in heating fees have been recalculated for periods when residents did not receive heat. An investigation by the Committee for the Development of Competition found that payments were charged even when heating facilities were non-operational due to repairs or disruptions. The recalculation benefits over 5,500 households.

item.title: Kazakhstan MFA Comments on Citizen Detained in Phuket
item.description: Kazakhstan's Ministry of Foreign Affairs has commented on the detention of a Kazakhstani citizen in Phuket, Thailand. The individual, who was internationally wanted, was apprehended by local law enforcement through Interpol based on a request from Kazakhstan's Prosecutor General's Office. Kazakhstan is working with authorities to extradite the detained person.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Mandates Parking Spaces in New Buildings Match Apartment Count
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Construction now requires new residential buildings to have a number of parking spaces equal to the number of apartments. This regulation applies to all new housing projects. The ministry emphasizes that permits will not be issued if this norm is not met.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Ministry Bans Apartment Sales Until Foundation Work is Complete
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Construction has introduced a ban on selling apartments and commercial spaces until the foundational "zero cycle" of construction is finished. Minister Nurdann Orundaev stated this aims to protect citizens' funds and reduce risks for buyers. The ministry wants developers to invest in construction first before profiting from sales.

item.title: Russia Cuts Healthcare Spending Amidst Rising Military Costs, Affecting Rural Access
item.description: Planned cuts to federal healthcare spending in Russia for 2027 are raising concerns about access to medical care, particularly in rural areas. A case in the Yaroslavl region highlights critical delays in emergency response and a lack of basic medical supplies. Funding for programs like "Active Longevity" may decrease significantly.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan Ministry Halts New Projects for 30 Construction Firms
item.description: Kyrgyzstan's Ministry of Construction has banned approximately 30 building companies from starting new projects until they complete existing ones. Minister Nurdann Oruntaev stated that some projects have been ongoing since 2020. The ministry will monitor progress daily and may involve law enforcement if deadlines are missed.

item.title: Kazakhstan's 'Burkit' Special Forces Welcomes First Female Combatant
item.description: For the first time, a female soldier has been accepted into the combat ranks of the 'Burkit' special forces unit of Kazakhstan's National Guard. Known by the call sign 'Kitana,' Kymbat impressed special unit soldiers at an international competition in Dubai, leading to her recruitment.

item.title: Kazakhstan Extradites Suspect from Georgia for Major Fraud Scheme
item.description: Kazakhstan's Prosecutor General's Office and National Security Committee extradited a citizen from Georgia suspected of large-scale fraud and manufacturing counterfeit medical supplies. The suspect allegedly organized a scheme to illegally obtain domestic producer status for tenders, causing over 4.5 billion tenge in damages to the state. He has been detained pending investigation.

item.title: Afghanistan Without Polio Urges Parents to Vaccinate Children Against Polio
item.description: Afghanistan Without Polio has urged parents to vaccinate their children against polio to protect them from the disease. The organization stated that the polio vaccination campaign was continuing and thanked parents for their cooperation. Polio is described as a dangerous, contagious viral disease primarily affecting children under five.

item.title: Kazakhstan Increases Threshold for Mobile Transfer Scrutiny by Tax Authorities
item.description: Kazakhstan has raised the threshold for mobile money transfers that will attract the attention of tax authorities. The new limit is 1,557,000 tenge per three months, up from the previous 1,020,000 tenge. The calculation method has also changed from minimum wages to monthly calculated indicators.

item.title: Suspect in Large-Scale Fraud Extradited to Kazakhstan from Georgia
item.description: A Kazakh citizen suspected of large-scale fraud and counterfeit medical product manufacturing has been extradited from Georgia to Kazakhstan. The suspect allegedly created a scheme to obtain domestic producer status for foreign medical equipment, causing over 4.5 billion tenge in damages. He is now in a pre-trial detention center.

item.title: Switzerland Removes Usmanov and Fridman from Sanctions List After EU
item.description: Following the European Union, Switzerland has also removed Russian businessmen Alisher Usmanov and Mikhail Fridman from its sanctions list. The Swiss government announced this decision, which aligns with the EU's 21st sanctions package against Russia and Belarus. The reasons for removing Usmanov and Fridman were not specified in the EU Council's document.

item.title: Suspect in 4.5 Billion Tenge Fraud Case Extradited from Georgia to Kazakhstan
item.description: A citizen of Kazakhstan suspected of large-scale fraud and manufacturing/selling counterfeit medical products has been extradited from Georgia. The General Prosecutor's Office reported that the damage to the state exceeded 4.5 billion tenge. The suspect allegedly organized a scheme to obtain domestic producer status for medical equipment without actual local production.

item.title: Tashkent Metro Discusses Cooling Systems, Security Barriers, and Five-Car Trains
item.description: Tashkent Metro's chief engineer stated that each carriage is designed for 300 passengers but often carries up to 500 during peak hours, causing inconvenience and affecting train movement. A press conference addressed rumors of high salaries and nepotism, with officials assuring that personnel matters and conflict of interest prevention are under strict control.

item.title: Kyrgyzstan President Proposes Ban on Energy Drinks Amid High Consumption
item.description: President Sadyr Japarov has proposed a ban on energy drinks in Kyrgyzstan, where an estimated 129 million cans are consumed annually. The production and import of these beverages will be reviewed as part of the proposed measure. Further details on the initiative are expected.

item.title: Tajik President Emomali Rahmon to Visit Kazakhstan for Official Talks
item.description: Tajikistan's President Emomali Rahmon will undertake an official visit to Kazakhstan from November 5-7, 2026, at the invitation of President Kassym-Jomart Tokayev. The leaders are scheduled to discuss further development of interstate cooperation and strengthening strategic partnership and alliance between the two nations.

item.title: Tashkent Construction Firm Fined 5.5 Billion Soums for Environmental Violations
item.description: A construction company in Tashkent has been ordered to pay 5.5 billion soums for environmental violations, including illegally cutting down 51 trees and polluting the environment. The National Committee for Ecology and Climate Change found that the company failed to meet requirements for dust control and waste disposal.

item.title: Mother of Four Found Dead in Aktobe; Ex-Partner Suspected of Murder
item.description: A 26-year-old woman died from stab wounds on November 3 in Aktobe, Kazakhstan, reportedly while attempting to register a new marriage. Her former partner is suspected of the murder following a dispute over parental rights. The suspect has been detained, and a criminal case has been initiated. The deceased leaves behind four children.

item.title: Samruk-Kazyna Head Warns of Personal Responsibility for Investment Project Delays
item.description: Nurlan Zhakupov, head of Samruk-Kazyna, emphasized personal accountability for meeting investment project deadlines during a meeting with portfolio company leaders. The discussion focused on timely commissioning of major projects, aligning with the President's goals for infrastructure modernization and new power generation.

item.title: Situation Center for Water Resource Data Collection and Analysis Opened in Astana
item.description: A new Situation Center has been established in Astana to facilitate the collection and analysis of data related to water resources. This initiative aims to improve the management and understanding of the region's water assets through centralized data processing and insights.

item.title: New Stadler Trains to Launch on Astana Routes Next Week
item.description: Stadler trains will begin operating on the Astana-Almaty and Astana-Semey routes starting next week. Ticket sales have opened, with daily services between Astana and Almaty from November 11 and services between Astana and Semey from November 13. The trains feature modern amenities and are designed for Kazakhstan's climate.

item.title: Pakistani Imarat Company May Participate in New Tashkent Projects
item.description: Pakistan's Imarat Company has been invited to explore opportunities in New Tashkent development projects. The construction firm, specializing in real estate management, sales, and digital customer service systems, is considering participation. Further details are available on Daryo.uz.

item.title: Over 135 Million Tenge Recovered from Alimony Debtors in Aktau
item.description: Aktau authorities have recovered approximately 135 million tenge from alimony debtors, seizing assets including two apartments, a land plot, and three cars. Additionally, 46 debtors faced administrative penalties for income concealment and evading parental duties, with 11 criminal cases initiated.

item.title: Kazakhstan Offers Three Pension Fund Investment Strategies to Contributors
item.description: Kazakhstanis can now choose from three investment strategies for their pension savings managed by private companies. Contributors can select conservative, balanced, or high-risk portfolios based on their proximity to retirement and risk tolerance. Previously, all clients' funds were invested in a single common portfolio.

item.title: Tashkent Metro Reports 353 Billion Som Revenue in 2025, Operates at a Loss
item.description: Tashkent Metro generated 353 billion som in passenger revenue in 2025, but its annual expenses exceeded 950 billion som, requiring state budget subsidies. The metro is considered a socially important, state-supported system, with passenger revenue covering only about one-third of its total costs. Major expenses include salaries and electricity.
